x↔y pairing of two tracks by charge: the simulation study

MX17 reconstruction paper, section "x↔y pairing" (nTof_x17 rerun/pairing_sim/PLAN.md). 2026-10-26. Data: the five bench chambers' golden rows, production final_phys tables. Simulation: MX17_Geant response chain, v4c (det3 conditions: wet gas, σ0 420 µm, bG 0.48, 26.5 mm column), reconstructed by the production wft with det3's golden-row phys bundle.

Verdict. The data side holds on every chamber: pairing by charge is 87–97 % right with charge alone and 90–98 % with the depth profile, and it gets worse where a chamber's x/y charge identity is looser (det6 σ = 0.18, det7 0.14 against det3 0.055). The response simulation fails the gate that matters: its single-track σ ln(q_x/q_y) is 0.101 against det3's 0.055 (×1.86), and its σ(u50_x − u50_y) is 137 ns against 93 ns (×1.48). Two causes, both in the simulation. (1) Stage B lands each avalanche, and all its feedback secondaries, at one point, so the x/y split samples the sub-pad split function once per primary electron: already at the induced-charge level (no electronics) the sim's split is 0.059 = 0.84/√N; displacing the feedback secondaries (a registered diagnostic) brings it to 0.035, as predicted. (2) The sim's waveforms carry more x/y scatter than the data's (model-free, same strips: 0.071–0.087 against 0.040–0.041), and production wft fits them worse than it fits data (fit 0.101 against 0.053; it stays at 0.095–0.108 when (1) is removed). Per PLAN §4 the sim goes back to MX17_Geant before S3–S5 numbers enter the paper. What the sim does give: the same mechanism (pairing fails only for near-equal charges), a both-found vs separation curve close to the data's, and a pessimistic bound — with twice the data's x/y spread the simulated overlay still pairs 84.2 % right (charge) and 90.8 % (charge + profile) at ≥ 24 mm, and 91.0 % / 91.0 % with the n_TOF noise floor (×2).

1 · The data gates, per chamber

Clean single tracks: interior M3 rays that production detects, with exactly one candidate in each view within 5 mm of the ray (det7 x: connectors 5–8 only). On det3 this is the same 5 882 tracks as the satstudy class-S selection. Toy: odd event ids calibrate the rule (median and robust σ of each x−y feature), even ids are paired at random (200 k pairs).

σ ln(q_x/q_y) is flat in track angle on every chamber and only 5–10 % of it is a position map (50 mm cells), so it is a per-track property. det4's broad Landau (σ ln Q 1.5) is its fixed amplification stripes; it helps pairing (fewer near-equal pairs). det6/det7 lose 6–9 points against det3 through their looser x/y identity; the mechanism of that (det6 and det7 share the 6-26 overnight, both have Y cross-card shorts) is not established here.

The sim reconstructed with its own sim-calibrated bundle (RECO_TRUTH) gives the same σ ln(q_x/q_y) (0.100 vs 0.101), so the choice of bundle is not the cause.

3 · Where the sim's x/y spread comes from

Left: the truth-level split (charge induced on all X vs all Y channels, before shaping and noise) narrows exactly as 1/√N with the number of electrons N reaching the mesh: each avalanche lands its whole charge (and, at H = 0, its feedback secondaries) at one point, so it contributes one random draw of the split. Right: the same strips (production footprint ± 3 mm), summed the same way, on data and sim: the data are 2× tighter at every level. The table follows the split through the chain: induced → waveform (model-free) → wft fit. Removing the per-avalanche coin (displaced secondaries) fixes the first step and part of the second, not the third: the fit adds ~0.08 in quadrature on the sim's waveforms against ~0.04 on the data's, the same direction as RECO_TRUTH's unexplained wft nonlinearity on simulated waveforms.

4 · Pairing right vs the two tracks' charge ratio

Data det3: 95.8 % (charge), 97.6 % (+ profile). Sim, pooled 0–15° points: 91.1 %, 91.2 %. In both, pairing fails only when |ln Q1/Q2| is below ~2σ(lq); the sim's curve is shifted to larger ratios by its wider σ, as expected, so the mechanism is reproduced and the number is not.

5 · S2: the overlay in the simulation, at bench and n_TOF noise

Two simulated single muons summed in the waveforms (b moved by whole strips to the drawn separation, added on its footprint ± 5 mm), seeded from 5σ hits of the sum and reconstructed by production wft; truth = each donor's own fit. n2: three more noise realisations on every strip (noise amplitude ×2, the post-23-July floor), seeding threshold and fit noise doubled. Pairing rule calibrated on the sim's own singles.

≥ 24 mm, both found: data 96.7 % / 100.0 %; sim 84.2 % / 90.8 % (n = 76); sim noise ×2 91.0 % / 91.0 % (n = 78). Doubling the noise does not move pairing (the two sim conditions agree within their ±4-point statistics): a MIP's charge is far above the noise in both views, so the charge ratio, not the noise, decides. Production's own beam-tuned pairing (track_id) is 28–34 % right here (50 % in the data overlay): its gate is beam-tuned.

6 · What this does not rule out, and what is left

  • The sim is not validated for pairing. Its x/y split is ~1.9× too wide and its u50/u90 spread ~1.5× too wide, so its pairing numbers are a lower bound, not a prediction. The Landau width passes once the data's own gain map is taken out (the sim muons cross one 31 mm spot).
  • n_TOF conditions are emulated by noise only: the beam gas (1.5 % H2O, ~160 ppm O2 attachment) needs a Stage B gas table with attachment that does not exist yet; attachment removes late charge from both views alike, so it should change the profile features more than the charge.
  • S3 (X17 / IPC e+e− pairs from a common vertex) and S5 (three tracks) are not run. The Stage A gun is ready (mm_sim --primaries-table, MX17_Geant), smoke-tested with 2- and 3-primary events; what is missing is a fixed sim (above) and the pair table from ipc_born.py with the n_TOF chamber geometry.
  • The data toy is at infinite separation; the overlay is the only measurement with merging and shared strips, and it is det3 only.
  • det6 / det7's wider x/y spread is measured, not explained.
